question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 4 & 3\end{bmatrix}$. Find all possible matrices $X$ such that $AX = XA$ and $X$ is a $2 \times 2$ matrix. Analyze the possible solutions, justifying each step logically.
explanation:
Let $X = \begin{bmatrix}a & b\\c & d\end{bmatrix}$

$AX = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 4 & 3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}a & b\\c & d\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}2a - c & 2b - d \\ 4a + 3c & 4b+3d\end{bmatrix}$

$XA = \begin{bmatrix}a & b\\c & d\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 4 & 3\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}2a+4b & -a+3b \\ 2c+4d & -c+3d\end{bmatrix}$

Equate:
$2a-c = 2a+4b \implies c = -4b$
$2b-d = -a+3b \implies 2b-d = -a+3b \implies a - d = 0\implies a = d$
$4a+3c = 2c+4d \implies 4a+3c = 2c+4d \implies 4a + 1c - 4d = 0 \implies 4a - 4d + c = 0$
But since $a = d$, $c=0$
But from first, $c = -4b$
So $c = 0 \implies b = 0$
So $b = 0$, $c = 0$, $a = d$

Check the last equation: $4b+3d = -c+3d$ gives $4b+3d = -c+3d \implies 4b = -c$ with $c=0$ so $b=0$

Thus, $X = \begin{bmatrix}a & 0\\0 & a\end{bmatrix} = aI$

So, only scalar multiples of identity matrix commute with $A$ in this case.
